players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: A week of 72–71 thrillers, mass Haaland hope and one bloke scoring 47 and feeling it
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 served everything except consistency. Patrick opened with the season-high 76, Woolly put a marker down with a 21-point wallop, Rob and Paul produced the highest-scoring, one-point thriller of the week, and Tom scored 47 — which is a number and also a mood. Plenty to mock, and even more to admire (briefly).

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 — Roped in again 71
matches.text: The match of the week and the highest-scoring tie (143 points) went right down to the wire. Rob (Humorous Name United) edged Paul (Roped in again) by a single point after both managers leaned on the same reliable bits of the game: João Pedro (11) appeared in both sides and both captains underwhelmed by FPL standards — Rob captained Bruno (2 → 4), Paul captained Haaland (2 → 4). Rob gets to celebrate a dramatic win; Paul gets to say he was unlucky, which is the agreed-upon behaviour in these situations.

matches.title: Richard 56 — Prince Majid Rd FC 57
matches.text: Rich (Richard) and Rami (Prince Majid Rd FC) produced a one-point squeaker in which the neatest detail is both teams actually captained the same player: Bruno for Rich (2 → 4) and Bruno for Rami (2 → 4). João Pedro again popped up with 11 for both sides. Rami somehow sneaks the win — helpful when you live in Saudi and can casually flex your fantasy luck.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 — Bielsa's Babes 76
matches.text: Patrick's 76 was the high score of the week and it arrived with the usual scattergun approach to points: Benjamin White 11, Ødegaard 11 and João Pedro 11 all helped. David (Change Name FC) pushed a respectable 67 but came up short — both managers had Haaland as captain and received the same underwhelming haul (2 → 4), so this one swung on the rest of the midfielders rather than a single superstar doing anything dramatic.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 — BeLucky Again 51
matches.text: Tom (el Guapo) recorded the week's low with 47 and will be getting text messages about 'wild start' for days. Both Tom and Kev (BeLucky Again) captained Haaland and both received the same modest return (2 → 4), but Kevin's bench and supporting cast just about scraped him past Tom by four. Not a disaster for Kev — more of a tidy Wednesday 18th-hole result, given he's usually off on a golf trip.

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 — Seattle Scorchers 50
matches.text: A draw. An actual 50–50. Rob (FC Dangerous) and Andrew (Seattle Scorchers) matched each other point-for-point in the narrowest possible margin: zero. Both had Haaland as captain (2 → 4) and João Pedro (11) on their teams, meaning neither could claim bragging rights except for the right to say 'at least I didn't lose.' Absolute parity, which in a league built on outrage is almost impressive.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 — Atletico Waspo 59
matches.text: Foz (Atletico Waspo) takes the four-point win over James (ChampagneSuperRovers). Again, Haaland captains were a theme — Ben had him (2 → 4) — and João Pedro (11) kept showing up for everyone. A tight little game that feels like the kind of match both managers will forget in two weeks and argue about forever.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 — Turf Less 50
matches.text: Woolly made the biggest statement of the week, beating Martyn (Turf Less) by the biggest margin: 21 points. Martyn did have Cole Palmer's 13 (the week's best single non-captain score) but it was nowhere near enough. Ben's team delivered across the board (João Pedro 11 again) and he strolls off with the weekend smugness only the properly wealthy can sustain.

awards.text: Highest score of the week (76). Patrick didn't need a miracle from Haaland — a spread of 11s (Benjamin White, Ødegaard, João Pedro) did the job. Enjoy being top of the pile for 48 hours.
Won the highest-scoring match of the week 72–71. Rob's lot get to keep the bragging rights for orchestrating a proper one-point victory — the most annoying kind to celebrate.
Lowest score of the week (47). Tom will insist this was tactical. The rest of us will point at the bench with Granit Xhaka still sitting pretty for a 9 that never counted.

Biggest winning margin (21) as Woolbrohampton thumped Turf Less 71–50. Ben gets to spend the rest of the week reminding anyone who'll listen that his team selection is as subtle as a mid-summer yacht purchase.

1.table_commentary: Using H2H points and the FPL tiebreaker (total points scored), Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) sits top after his 76, with Rob (Humorous Name United) and Woolly (Woolbrohampton) filling out the top three on the tie-breakers. Six teams picked up three points this week, so the table is crowded at the top and will sort itself out soon — particularly where those who scored in the low 70s lose out to Patrick’s 76. Martyn (Turf Less) finds himself bottom after that 50, while Tom (el Guapo) will be spending the week trying to remember where he left his optimism.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC vs Woolbrohampton
preview.text: Rami (Prince Majid Rd FC) travels to face Woolly. Ben's 71 was impressive, and Rami will fancy himself after squeaking past Rich. If Rami wants to keep up with Ben on FPL points, he'll need more than João Pedro and a neat defensive return.

Martyn (Turf Less) tries to recover from that 21-point reverse against James (ChampagneSuperRovers). Martyn's Cole Palmer gave him a rare bright spot — if he can find another one he might escape the bottom of the table next week.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes vs Humorous Name United
preview.text: Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) faces Rob (Humorous Name United) in a tasty early-season tie. Both managers opened strongly; this one could be decided by which of them remembers to bench the bloke on eight points and play the one on eleven.

1.closing: That's your lot for GW1: plenty of tight finishes, a couple of clean sheets on the scoreboard and one manager who went home with a proper mattress of points. Enjoy the arguments, the transfers and Kev's inevitable weekday golf excuse. See you for GW2.
